label: Tools
title: Tools Settings
subtitle: Install, configure, and connect tools available to all agents.
description: The Tools tab manages which tools are installed and active across the platform. Tools become available to agents once installed; individual agents choose which installed tools they can use.

settings.name: Installed Tools
settings.description: Lists every active tool with its version and a remove button. Click a tool to configure its global defaults.

settings.name: Tool Settings
settings.description: Tools that expose configurable settings (for example the web search result limit, the download size cap, or a default LaTeX engine) show a form when you click Configure. The values you set here become the defaults for every agent. Each field is validated against the tool's declared limits, so an out-of-range value is rejected before it is saved.

settings.name: Per-Agent Overrides
settings.description: Below the shared settings, pick an agent to give it its own values for the same tool — useful when one agent should, say, return more search results or use a longer timeout than the rest. An agent's override wins over the shared default; clearing it falls back to the default.

settings.name: Available Tools
settings.description: Built-in tool catalog. Click Install to add a tool to your instance.

settings.name: Remote MCP Servers
settings.description: Add connections to external MCP servers by entering their endpoint URL and any required credentials.

mediaCaption: The Tools tab on the Installed sub-tab, showing active tools with version numbers and remove buttons
tips: Removing a tool from this panel disables it for every agent immediately — agents that relied on it will lose that capability until you reinstall it.

Tool settings cascade: a project can override the global defaults from its own Settings → Tools tab, and a per-agent override is the most specific of all. The effective value for any tool call is resolved from the most specific layer that sets it.
Use Remote MCP Servers to connect proprietary internal tools without publishing them anywhere.
